messages.author: 059504e415ddf983
messages.subject: Re: Question about Kronecker product models
parts:
Hi Jonas,

we have used the Kronecker product models not in the SPDE context but for correlating smoothing priors
or overdispersion parameters, see http://arxiv.org/abs/1108.0606. We specified for example a random
walk over time for each of several geographical regions and then correlated them based on a Kronecker product
of a uniform correlation matrix and the structure matrix of the random walk.  This was useful on
one side to get more precise estimates and on the other side to improve the imputation of data missing
in one geographical region. We implemented this feature in INLA using the group-ing option. The R-code used
for the paper is posted on http://lib.stat.cmu.edu/aoas/498/. However, I will also try to
post a simple example on the r-inla website.

Hope this helps.

Best regards
Andrea

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: Question about Kronecker product models
parts:
Further to what Andrea said, there are currently only two models that can be used in Kronecker models: the exchangeable model and the AR(1) model.  I've used  SPDE \otimes AR(1) as a space-time model, but in principle it will work with any "left hand" latent model (BYM, RW2, etc).  An example is in the paper by Cameletti et al, which is in the "Papers" section.

To the best of my knowledge, there are plans for a general Kronecker product mechanism in INLA, however this has not been started yet.

Best,

Dan
